title: How About a Nice Game of Chess?
description: Brute‑force MD5 hashing to discover an 8‑character door password.
writeup:
## Approach

This puzzle is a pure brute‑force MD5 search. For both parts, we repeatedly compute MD5 hashes of the Door ID concatenated with an increasing integer index. A hash is considered "interesting" when it begins with five zeroes in hexadecimal. Part 1 extracts characters sequentially; Part 2 uses the hash to determine both position and character.

The challenge is computational rather than algorithmic: millions of hashes must be computed. The logic is simple, but performance matters.

## Part 1

We iterate index values starting from 0. For each MD5 hash of `door_id + index`, if the hash starts with `00000`, the sixth character (`hash[5]`) is appended to the password. We stop once we have 8 characters.

This produces the password in strict discovery order.

## Part 2

Part 2 changes the rule: the sixth character of the hash (`hash[5]`) is interpreted as a *position* (0–7), and the seventh character (`hash[6]`) is the value to place there. We only fill a position once.

We continue hashing until all 8 positions are filled. Invalid positions (non‑digits or out of range) are ignored.

The result is an order‑independent password built by positional placement rather than sequential discovery.
